cli.conversation.noDelegator: This delegation didn't record the conversation that started it; use --session
cli.conversation.notUpstream: This tmux is neither a branch line nor a delegate; use --session
cli.credentials.hashed: The password is stored only as a scrypt hash; the plain text isn't kept in the file.
cli.credentials.restart: Restart the backend (for example {command}) to use the new login.
cli.credentials.restartGeneric: Restart the backend to use the new login.

cli.delegate.blocked: The user was told (delegation {id} needs attention). Carry on once they answer.
cli.delegate.delivered: Delivered delegation {id}; waiting for the user's review.
cli.delegate.deliveredForReview: Delivered delegation {id}; the delegating LLM reviews it first, then the user; feedback on a send-back arrives here.
cli.delegate.passed: Reviewed delegation {id}; the user reviews it in the app.
cli.delegate.proposed: Delegation proposed; waiting for the user to approve it in the app (to {profile}). The result comes back to this conversation by itself; status: hestia delegate status {id}
cli.delegate.roundsUsed: No send-backs left; delegation {id} went to the user for review.
cli.delegate.sentBack: Sent delegation {id} back (round {round}). The feedback goes in once the delegate is idle; its next delivery comes back to this conversation.
cli.delegate.started: Delegated to {profile}. The result comes back to this conversation by itself once delivered; status: hestia delegate status {id}
cli.delegate.stopped: Stopped delegation {id} ({state}). The delegate's tmux and working folder are kept.
cli.open.manyProjects: This folder belongs to more than one project:
cli.open.newProject: This folder isn't in any project yet. New project name (Enter for "{folder}"):

cli.pair.openInApp: Or open it in the installed Hestia app:
cli.pair.openInBrowser: Or open it in the phone's browser:
cli.pair.reach: The phone must be able to reach {url}.
cli.pair.reachTailscale: The phone needs the Tailscale app, logged in to the same account as this host.
cli.pair.revokeAsk: Not you? Type r to revoke this login, or press Enter to finish:
cli.pair.revokeMissing: That login wasn't found; it may have logged out already.
cli.pair.revokedDetail: : that device has to log in again.

cli.pair.secret: • It is as good as a login to this host; don't photograph it or send it to anyone.

cli.sshAuthorize.added: ✓ Added the key {fingerprint}: it can only reach this Hestia (port {port}).
cli.sshAuthorize.cleanupFailed: The one-time line (ending in {comment}) couldn't be removed from authorized_keys. It stops working by itself in a few minutes; delete it when you can.
cli.sshAuthorize.confirm: Does the app show the same fingerprint? Add this key to {user}'s authorized_keys, allowed only to reach port {port}? [y/N]
cli.sshAuthorize.expired: Time's up; nothing was added. Run it again to try again.
cli.sshAuthorize.file.changed: authorized_keys ({path}) changed while it was being written; nothing was written. Try again.
cli.sshAuthorize.file.dirMode: {path} can be written by group or others; sshd ignores keys in it. Nothing was changed. To fix it:
cli.sshAuthorize.file.dirOwner: {path} belongs to another user; sshd won't use it. Fix its owner first (nothing was changed).
cli.sshAuthorize.file.dirSymlink: {path} is a symbolic link; it's left alone. Point it at a real directory, or add the key yourself.
cli.sshAuthorize.file.locked: Another hestia ssh-authorize is writing authorized_keys ({path}); try again in a moment.
cli.sshAuthorize.file.mode: {path} can be written by group or others; sshd ignores it. Nothing was changed. To fix it:
cli.sshAuthorize.file.notUtf8: {path} holds bytes that aren't UTF-8; to leave the other lines exactly as they are, nothing was changed. Add the line by hand instead.
cli.sshAuthorize.file.owner: {path} belongs to another user; sshd won't use it. Fix its owner first (nothing was changed).
cli.sshAuthorize.file.symlink: {path} is a symbolic link; it's left alone. Add the key to the file it points to yourself.
cli.sshAuthorize.file.verifyFailed: The new authorized_keys ({path}) wasn't exactly the old one plus the change, so it wasn't written.
cli.sshAuthorize.keyUnsupported: That isn't a key this command adds: it takes ssh-ed25519, or ssh-rsa of 2048 bits or more, as 'type base64 [name]'.
cli.sshAuthorize.link: Or paste this link in the app:
cli.sshAuthorize.merged: ✓ The key {fingerprint} was already here; it may now reach port {port} too.
cli.sshAuthorize.needsTerminal: This needs a terminal: you confirm the phone's key here by typing y. Without one, use --public-key.
cli.sshAuthorize.noAddress: No address for the phone to reach this machine at was found; pass one with --address.
cli.sshAuthorize.noHostKeys: No ed25519 or ECDSA host key could be read in {dir}, so the app couldn't check it is talking to this machine.
cli.sshAuthorize.noPairingCode: The key was added, but Hestia's API didn't give a pairing code (is it running?). Log in in the app with your password, or run hestia pair.
cli.sshAuthorize.otherKeysFile: sshd's AuthorizedKeysFile ({path}) doesn't include ~/.ssh/authorized_keys, so a key written there wouldn't be used. Add the key to the file it names yourself.
cli.sshAuthorize.presentOther: The key {fingerprint} is already here with options Hestia didn't write, so nothing was changed. If it should reach Hestia (port {port}), the line Hestia would use is:
cli.sshAuthorize.presentUnrestricted: The key {fingerprint} is already allowed here without restrictions, so nothing was changed. To let it reach only Hestia, replace its line with:
cli.sshAuthorize.remoteLoginHint: On a Mac: System Settings › General › Sharing › Remote Login.
cli.sshAuthorize.root: Don't run this as root: the key is added for the account Hestia runs as. Run it as that user.
cli.sshAuthorize.scan: In the Hestia app: Add host › SSH › Scan, and scan this to allow the phone's key here:
cli.sshAuthorize.secret: • Anyone who sees this code can send a key; compare the fingerprint below with the one the app shows.
cli.sshAuthorize.sshdTooOld: This sshd ({banner}) isn't OpenSSH 7.7 or newer, which the one-time key needs (expiry-time). Use --public-key with the key the app shows instead.
cli.sshAuthorize.sshdUnreachable: Nothing answers SSH at 127.0.0.1:{port}. The phone connects through this machine's sshd, so it has to be running (pass --ssh-port if it listens elsewhere).
cli.sshAuthorize.validFor: • Works for {minutes} minutes, for one key. You'll be asked here before anything is added.
cli.sshAuthorize.waiting: Waiting for the app… (Ctrl-C to quit)
